sections.h2: Where do you find the Perry County recorder?
sections.html:
Look for the recorder at 212 S. Main Street, New Lexington, where the doors are open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm and the number is (740) 342-2494. The Perry County Auditor shares that address and those hours.

The county's page frames the office as the place that keeps land records in an organized, accessible form: who owns what, how title moved, and which mortgages exist. Staff will not run a title search for you or advise you on legal questions. They will let you sit down and search the public records yourself.

Payment is by cash or check. Cards are not taken, so settle that before you send paperwork.

The recorder's fax line is (740) 342-5539, and the auditor can be reached at (740) 342-2074. If you are sorting out several documents for one sale, calling both offices on the same day saves a second trip.

sections.h2: What are the Perry County recording charges?
sections.html:
The recorder's FAQ spells out the price: $34.00 buys the first two pages and each page beyond costs $8.00. If the document ignores the margin rules, $20.00 is added, and a document that needs a cross-reference picks up $4.00.

Charges as posted on the Perry County Recorder page
SituationCharge
Pages one and two$34.00
Every further page$8.00
Top margin under 3 inches on page one, or sides and bottom under 1 inch$20.00 added
Cross-reference to an earlier record$4.00 added
Accepted paymentCash or check

State law in Revised Code 317.32 allows counties to add a preservation surcharge up to $5. The Perry page lists none, so ask the office whether one applies to your filing.

sections.h2: What does the Perry County auditor collect on a sale?
sections.html:
Ahead of recording, the auditor moves the parcel into the buyer's name on the tax list. The buyer or the buyer's representative files a statement of value, and the seller owes the conveyance fee.

Statute 319.54(G)(3) sets the state portion at one dollar, or ten cents per hundred dollars of value (rounded up for any fraction), whichever is greater. Section 322.02 lets a county commissioners' board levy a transfer tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars on top, so what you owe at the table depends on Perry County's own resolutions.

The auditor's site hosts a Conveyance Fee Calculator that builds in the per-parcel transfer fee: key in the number of parcels and the price. State conveyance forms sit on the Forms page of the same site.

sections.h2: How can you search Perry County land records?
sections.html:
An online index named Adaptable Visual Access returns the volume and page for each recorded item. Images of the documents are not posted there, so call or write to the office to order a copy and learn the fee and payment options.

The office also sets owners up with a free fraud alert through its software vendor. A subscriber is told within 24 business hours when anything is recorded under their name. Because the office has to record any paper that meets the filing rules, the alert warns you but cannot block a filing.

Veterans can have a DD214 recorded by bringing the original or a certified copy and photo ID, and the office hands out veteran ID cards too.

sections.h2: What else does the Perry County recorder file?
sections.html:
Revised Code 317.08 sends a long list of instruments into the official records. The following matter most to someone selling a house:

  • Mortgages and their modifications.
  • Land installment contracts that run beyond a year, plus leases.
  • Powers of attorney, used when an agent signs for the seller.
  • Mechanic's liens, federal tax liens and similar recorded claims.
  • Purchase options, accepted only when they give an expiration day and year.

Paper goes on record in the sequence it arrives. An owner's transfer on death affidavit is filed like a deed, at the deed price, and counts only if recorded before death.

sections.h2: What should a Perry County seller fix before recording?
sections.html:
Most trouble traces to small slips. Run through this list before signing:

  • An officer listed in section 5301.01, such as a notary, witnesses your signature and certifies the acknowledgment.
  • The new owner's mailing address and a cite to the preceding recorded deed appear on the face of the deed, as section 319.20 expects.
  • Margins follow the layout rules, which avoids the $20.00 add-on.
  • You hold the lender's payoff figure. Once paid, the lender sends a release for recording, and the recorder can hand you a copy.
  • You can pay by check or cash.

When a spouse has died and a name has to come off the deed, remember the recorder records but does not draft. An attorney writes the instrument.

sections.h2: How does Perry County housing look in the Census data?
sections.html:
An estimated 35,918 people lived in Perry County in July 2025, 1.4% above the April 2020 estimates base, on about 408 square miles of land. The Census Bureau reports 15,173 housing units and 13,452 households.

  • Homes occupied by owners: 76.4%.
  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $191,100.
  • Gross rent at the midpoint: $777 monthly.
  • Average trip to work: 33.2 minutes.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 39.
  • Residents below the poverty line: 13.7%.

That 33.2 minute average is the longest of the three counties in the Census table, and Wikipedia lists Perry County in the Columbus metropolitan area.

On the income side, the same table shows household income at the midpoint of $67,460 and per capita income of $32,288 for 2020 to 2024. Employers numbered 455 in 2023, and employment of 4,478 grew 5.0% over 2022. Retail sales in 2022 came to $6,963 per resident, and 16.2% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

sections.h2: How does the Perry County auditor value property?
sections.html:
According to the auditor, Ohio demands a full reappraisal of the county every six years, with a state percentage adjustment in the third year of each cycle. Roughly 31,000 parcels were on the books for 2024, sorted into residential, agricultural, commercial and industrial classes.

The auditor's home page also reports that House Bill 479 gives a one-time fixed reduction to current Standard and Enhanced Homestead Exemption recipients, for tax year 2026 or tax year 2027 on manufactured and mobile homes. If you are selling in the middle of a tax year, ask how that reduction carries over.

When storm or flood damage lowers what a house is worth, phone the auditor at (740) 342-2074 and ask how a damaged-property adjustment works.

sections.h2: What communities are in Perry County?
sections.html:
The state formed Perry County on March 1, 1818 out of parts of Fairfield, Washington and Muskingum counties. New Lexington serves as county seat and is the largest city. Villages include Corning, Crooksville, Glenford, Hemlock, Junction City, New Straitsville, Rendville, Roseville (partly here), Shawnee, Somerset and Thornville.

A section of Wayne National Forest falls within the county. Licking, Muskingum, Morgan, Athens, Hocking and Fairfield counties ring it.

faqs.q: Are credit cards accepted at the Perry County recorder?
faqs.a: No. The office takes cash and checks only, according to its own page.

faqs.q: Are Perry County deeds viewable online?
faqs.a: Only the index is online, giving volume and page numbers. The document images are not posted, so contact the recorder to order a copy.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Perry County?
faqs.a: The recorder quotes $34.00 for the first two pages plus $8.00 for each added page. Documents with bad margins pick up $20.00, and ones needing a reference pick up $4.00.

faqs.q: Where is the Perry County conveyance fee figured out?
faqs.a: On the Conveyance Fee Calculator at the auditor's website, which folds in the parcel transfer fee. The auditor's office at 212 S. Main Street can confirm the result.

faqs.q: Will the recorder confirm that my title is free of liens?
faqs.a: No. Staff do not search titles or give legal advice. Search the public records in person, or hire an attorney or title company.
